findings.title: "managed file" is used as a settled term of art well before it is ever defined
locations: src/CLI/Preflight.jl:804: "Returns true when no pinned or managed file is modified." (torn_check docstring)
src/CLI/Preflight.jl:844: "a pinned or managed file is modified in the working tree (CFG.TORN)"
src/CLI/Rounds.jl:68: "CFG.TORN — a pinned or managed file is modified in the working tree"
contrast: src/CLI/Sync.jl:8: "a managed file is one the tool renders into the consumer and hash-checks thereafter, edited only by `gbg sync`, never by hand" (the only definition in the whole source)
findings.description: The package's own module map (`?GBGCodingTools`) walks the reader through the modules in a fixed narrative order — main/Config/makedocs, then Preflight, Rounds, Passes, demote, Seeds, Recall, RoundFiles, Git, then only later Sync, Init, Ledger, Doctor. `Preflight.torn_check` (bulleted 4th) uses the phrase "a pinned or managed file" as if the reader already knows what a 'managed file' is, but the only place that ordinary English word is ever given a package-specific meaning is `Sync`'s module docstring (bulleted 8th, much later in the map). A cold reader who does `?GBGCodingTools.torn_check` or `?GBGCodingTools.preflight` at the point the map hands it to them has no way to know whether 'managed' means 'tracked by the tool', 'tool-owned', 'rendered', or something else — the very distinction Sync later goes out of its way to make precise (managed = tool-rendered and hash-checked, versus a file that is merely hand-written and must not drift). RULE.DOC.TERMS_DEFINED requires a term of art to be defined or linked at its first mention; here it is neither.
findings.resolution_hint: Either move a one-clause gloss of "managed file" into `torn_check`'s own docstring (or `@ref`-link `Sync`'s module docstring there), or reorder the module map so `Sync` is introduced before any docstring uses the bare phrase "managed file".

findings.title: "pinned file" (as opposed to "managed file") is never defined in any docstring at all
locations: src/CLI/Doctor.jl:228-234: `function pinned_and_managed(ctx)` — no docstring; builds the watched-file list (`.gbg/config.toml`, `.gbg/exemptions.toml`, `.gbg/seeds.toml`, `.gbg/managed.json`, `.gbg/hats/*.toml`, every sub-environment `Project.toml`) with zero surrounding prose
src/CLI/Doctor.jl:242: pass("CFG.TORN", "no pinned or managed file modified")
findings.description: "pinned" is first grounded, very early, as "a consumer pins the tool to one exact version" (GBGCodingTools.jl module docstring). "a pinned or managed file" reuses the same ordinary adjective for an entirely different, third concept: a fixed list of consumer-owned files (config, ledger, seed catalogue, the sync sidecar, hat personas, sub-environment manifests) that the tool never renders (so they are not 'managed' in Sync's sense) but that must still never be hand-edited outside their own write path. This category exists ONLY inside the private, undocumented helper `pinned_and_managed` — there is no docstring anywhere in src/ or ext/ that states what makes a file 'pinned' in this sense, or that this is a third sense of the word distinct from 'pinned version'. A cold reader can eventually reconstruct 'managed' from Sync's docstring, but has no textual source at all for 'pinned' (file-sense) — they would have to read the private function's code to learn the category exists.
findings.resolution_hint: Give `pinned_and_managed` a docstring naming the category explicitly (e.g. 'the files a consumer writes by hand once and the tool must never see drift on, as opposed to a managed file the tool itself renders'), and reference it from `torn_check`'s and CFG.TORN's prose.

findings.title: Half the act/state verdict vocabulary is glossed, half is bare, in the same enumeration
locations: src/CLI/Passes.jl:9-13: "...in a closed vocabulary: `HONORED` (the ask landed by the right means...), `LINE-ONLY` (the instance is fixed, the class is alive), `ADJACENT`, `INSERTED`, `NEW-DEFECT`, `SCOPE-CREEP`, `UNDONE` (nothing in the diff addresses it) and `LAUNDERED` (closed by declaring it acceptable);"
src/CLI/Passes.jl:14-16: "...grades whether the defect is in the tree now: `PRESENT` (its default), `PARTIAL`, `REGRESSED`, `ABSENT`, `NOT-A-DEFECT` or `UNCLEAR`."
findings.description: In the very same sentence, `HONORED`, `LINE-ONLY`, `UNDONE`, `LAUNDERED` (act) and `PRESENT`, `ABSENT`, `NOT-A-DEFECT` (state) each get a parenthetical gloss, but `ADJACENT`, `INSERTED`, `NEW-DEFECT`, `SCOPE-CREEP` (act) and `PARTIAL`, `REGRESSED`, `UNCLEAR` (state) get none anywhere in src/ or ext/ (confirmed by grep — these seven tokens appear nowhere else with explanatory prose). These are exactly the ordinary-English-word case the lane is built to catch: 'adjacent', 'inserted', 'scope-creep' and 'partial' all read as self-evident, but the whole point of a closed verdict vocabulary is that a reader must be able to tell them apart from their neighbours (e.g. what distinguishes an `ADJACENT` fix from an `INSERTED` one, or a `PARTIAL` state from `UNCLEAR`) — and nothing in the Julia source says. A cold reader is left to guess at exactly the half of the vocabulary that determines whether a finding closes, regresses, or is scope-creep.
findings.resolution_hint: Give each of the seven bare tokens the same one-clause parenthetical treatment their siblings already have in the same docstring.

findings.title: "swept" is used in Passes' docstring one module before it is defined in Demote's
locations: src/CLI/Passes.jl:10: "...whether the diff swept it)..." (inside the `class_surfaces` gloss)
src/CLI/Demote.jl:11: "...each marked `swept` when the fix pass's diff fixed the class there." (the only definition)
findings.description: The module map bullets Passes immediately before demote, so a cold reader following the map meets the technical sense of 'swept' (an ordinary word for 'this class of defect was fixed at this surface too') in Passes' own docstring one step before demote's docstring spells it out. The gap is small and the meaning is largely recoverable from context ('whether the diff swept it'), so this is a minor instance of the same pattern as the two managed/pinned-file findings above, not a blocking one.
findings.resolution_hint: Either gloss 'swept' inline in Passes' module docstring, or move its definition into Passes rather than Demote.
